title: Exec iterative ask archive & tone guidelines (Q3 prep)
content:
Purpose: quick, living notebook for collating executive asks, short OKR drafts, and rules-of-thumb for tone and comms ahead of Q3 all-hands. Focus is to make the slate small, defensible, and easy for execs to rehearse.

Status: Draft — rough collection from prior leadership syncs, product intake, and a couple of skip-level notes. This is intentionally scrappy: use as a source of truth for rehearsal and as an input for the final runbook.

Key constraints we keep repeating:
- Keep the number of exec asks <= 5 (primary + 2 backups + 2 cross-org asks).
- Tie each ask to a measurable signal (metric / milestone / deadline).
- Frame tradeoffs, not just requests (what we will deprioritize if we take this on).

Top-level proposed executive asks (short form):
1) Dedicated capacity acceleration: commit to +15% Dedicated capacity budget for Q3 (owner: VP Ops). Signal: guaranteed 99th p latency under 300ms for our 3 top customer tenants by Oct 15.
2) Private deployment partnerships: greenlight two pilot agreements with regulated customers and add headcount for onboarding (owner: Head of Sales + Solutions Eng). Signal: 2 signed MoUs by Nov 1.
3) Observability retention increase: approve +30 day window for route-level traces for paid tiers (owner: Product Console). Signal: pilot roll to 3 customers and initial cost offset plan.
4) Invest in model-eval automation: one fulltime SRE/ML infra hire to support continuous eval pipelines (owner: Applied ML). Signal: automated regression alerts running in staging by end of Q3.
5) Cross-org developer experience sprint: short program to reduce 'first-call-to-response' time by 20% (owner: DevEx). Signal: sample onboarding flows measured in minutes.

Messaging tone & rules (for execs):
- Principle: assume technical literacy, but prioritize crisp outcome language. Avoid product jargon in open-all-hands; use it in smaller ops briefings.
- Show one metric up front, then one anecdote that illustrates user impact. Example: "Latency dropped 40% for X product; as a result, checkout conversions improved by Y% for customer Z."
- When asking for resources: present the ask, the minimal success criteria, and the intended de-prioritization.

Rehearsal checklist (for execs):
- 1 week before: 15-min dry run with comms/ops; confirm fallback lines for 3 high-risk Qs.
- 3 days before: rehearse transitions between speakers on stage; confirm slide timing.
- Day of: on-site mic/AV check + 10-min green room.

Run-of-show (compact):
- 0:00–0:05 CEO: narrative + one metric (north star).
- 0:05–0:15 Product: demo highlight + user story + ask 1.
- 0:15–0:25 Infra & Reliability: SLO status + ask 2 + contingency.
- 0:25–0:35 Growth & GTM: key wins + product-market movement + ask 3.
- 0:35–0:50 Panel (leadership): short Q&A, scripted fallback answers for known hotspots.
- 0:50–1:00 Close: commitment and next steps.

Sample Q&A hotspots and suggested responses (bullet):
- "How will increased Dedicated capacity affect price?" -> "We will pilot allocation to enterprise tenants with committed revenue; plan includes cost-offset through reserved pricing."
- "What if model regressions increase with faster rollouts?" -> "We are putting automated eval gates and canary model traffic limits in place; fallback to prior model is automated."
- "How do private deployments affect our support SLAs?" -> "We will operate under a separate contract with dedicated onboarding and extended support windows."

OKR sketch (to be refined into final OKR format):
- Objective: Make Redwood the most predictable inference platform for early-stage AI product teams.
  - KR1: Reduce 95th-p latency for hosted API (small-medium requests) by 25% by EOY.
  - KR2: Achieve two Dedicated customers at >$25k/mo committed capacity by end of Q3.
  - KR3: Ship model-eval automation with 3 regression test suites in pipeline by Q4 kickoff.

Open questions / parking lot (notes to self):
- Do we need a separate legal checklist for Private pilot customers (ask Legal: Priya Shah).
- Can Finance model the Dedicated commit economics under 12-months and 24-months scenarios (Jira FIN-112).
- Validate cost of 30-day trace retention with infra (SRE: Carlos M.).

Action items (owners & ETA):
- Pull final metrics to show: VP Product (Lena) — due 2026-02-20.
- Draft exec speaking notes + 2 fallback paragraphs: Comms (Asha) — due 2026-02-25.
- Finalize slide deck and rehearsal schedule: Ops (Ravi) — due 2026-02-28.

Tone examples (do / don't):
- DO: "We saw a reproducible 18% improvement in latency for multi-tenant workloads; this helped customer Y reduce page load errors."
- DON'T: "We’re shipping a transformative, paradigm-shifting, market-disrupting infra change." (too hypey)

Quick history & context (pull-through):
- This doc aggregates asks surfaced during the Jan–Mar leadership sprints and the Feb offsite. It’s intentionally conservative compared to the original Q4 wishlist.

If you edit this doc: add a one-line rationale for any new ask and tag the owner. Keep the language short; the final runbook will be consolidated into the all-hands slide deck repo.

—— End —

Notes to self: next step — convert this into a 2-page runbook and a 1-slide executive ask summary. Also schedule a 30-minute rehearsal with the CEO and two execs the week before the all-hands.
